title: Adding forces that point in different directions
canonical_question: How do you add two forces that point in different directions to get the net force?
summary: Every force has a size and a direction, so two forces pointing different ways cannot simply be added as plain numbers.
For two forces from the same point you can draw a parallelogram with the forces as sides; the diagonal is the net force.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Forces are vectors
sections.body_md: Every force has a size and a direction, so two forces pointing different ways cannot simply be added as plain numbers. You place them tip to tail and the single arrow from the first tail to the last tip is their sum. That sum is the net force, and its direction can differ from either original force.

sections.heading: The parallelogram shortcut
sections.body_md: For two forces from the same point you can draw a parallelogram with the forces as sides; the diagonal is the net force. If the two forces are at right angles you can use the Pythagorean theorem for the size and the tangent for the angle. Either way you keep direction, not just magnitude.

key_points: Forces add as vectors, tip to tail, not as plain numbers.
The diagonal of the parallelogram is the net force.
core.bridge_to_parent: This shows the mechanics behind the net force the objective defines.
